items.stem: A clinician fixes on the first plausible diagnosis and stops considering others. Which reasoning error is this?

options.rationale: Correct: anchoring is premature fixation on an initial diagnosis without weighing alternatives.
Randomised control is a study design, not a reasoning error.
Herd immunity is a population-immunity concept, unrelated here.
Pharmacokinetics concerns drug handling, not diagnostic reasoning.

items.stem: What best distinguishes a screening test from a diagnostic test?

options.text: Screening is only done in hospitals
options.rationale: Setting does not define screening vs diagnosis.

options.text: Screening is applied to asymptomatic people to detect risk or early disease
options.rationale: Correct: screening targets asymptomatic individuals, whereas diagnostic testing evaluates symptomatic presentations.
Cost does not define the distinction.
Screening identifies risk; confirmation requires diagnostic testing.

items.stem: Which TWO principles support evidence-based practice for a nurse practitioner?

options.text: Integrating best available evidence with clinical expertise and patient values
options.rationale: Correct: this is the core definition of evidence-based practice.

options.text: Preferring high-quality guidelines over a single anecdote
options.rationale: Correct: weighting stronger evidence appropriately is central to EBP.

options.text: Following whichever option is cheapest regardless of evidence
options.rationale: Cost alone is not an EBP principle.

items.explanation: Correct: this is the core definition of evidence-based practice.
